title: LLMs Generate Structurally Realistic Social Networks But Overestimate Political Homophily

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring political homophily by calculating observed-to-expected cross-group edge ratios, isolation indices, and polarization metrics in LLM-generated social networks, as well as analyzing political stereotyping in LLM-generated persona interests.
Measuring gender homophily by calculating the ratio of observed-to-expected cross-group edges (friendships) between different genders in zero-shot LLM-generated social networks.
Measuring racial and ethnic homophily by calculating the ratio of observed-to-expected cross-group edges between different racial/ethnic demographic groups in zero-shot LLM-generated social networks.
Measuring religious homophily by calculating the ratio of observed-to-expected cross-group edges between different religious identities in zero-shot LLM-generated social networks.
Measuring age homophily by calculating the ratio of observed-to-expected average age gaps and cross-group edges between different age cohorts in zero-shot LLM-generated social networks.
